name: Djibouti
headline: Djibouti: +4.9% growth in 2025, −0.3% inflation, debt 31% of GDP
sections: Djibouti is a $4.5 billion economy (2025), the world's 178th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.9% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $8,452 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 5.3% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose −0.3% in 2025, in deflation, down from 5.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 26.0% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 76.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 31% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 42% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.4% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +14.5% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 206% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 16% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 66.2 years (2024). Population: 1.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
